preconditions.description: The input s must be a string.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(c, str) and len(c) == 1 for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: The return value is a list of single-character strings.
Every character in the result appears an odd number of times in the input string.

postconditions.expression: all(c in s for c in return_value) and len(set(return_value)) == len(return_value)
postconditions.description: The result contains only characters present in the input, with no duplicates.

postconditions.expression: all(s.count(c) % 2 == 1 for c in s) == (len(return_value) == len(set(s)))
postconditions.description: The result contains exactly the set of all characters that appear an odd number of times in the input.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] != return_value[j] for i in range(len(return_value)) for j in range(i + 1, len(return_value)))
postconditions.description: The result list contains unique characters.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value.index(c) < return_value.index(d) if (s.rfind(c) < s.rfind(d)) else True for i, c in enumerate(return_value) for j, d in enumerate(return_value) if i < j)
postconditions.description: The characters in the result are ordered by the index of their last occurrence in the input string, from earliest to latest.
